title: Proof that transient terms localise (categorical)
html:
Proof. The transient component \alpha - \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha) lies in \mathcal{A}_{n+1}^{\mathrm{trans}} = \ker\hat{\tau}_n. By the structure of the brane boundary, the support of a transient endomorphism is contained in the union of the kernels \ker(\mathfrak{d}_{n+1}|_{p_i}) at the blow-up centres p_1, \ldots, p_N. These kernels are mutually disjoint submodules because each arises from a distinct extension step. The transient trace therefore decomposes as a sum:

  \mathrm{tr}(\alpha - \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha))
  = 
  \sum_{i=1}^{N} \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{trans}}(\varrho, p_i).

The disjointness of the supports ensures that the norm of the sum equals the sum of the norms. \square
heading: Proof
